style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: A maskil with a betrayal in its title. The men of Ziph went to Saul twice -- once from the wilderness strongholds, once from the hill of Hachilah -- and said, 'Is David not hiding among us?' (1 Samuel 23:19; 26:1). David's answer is not a complaint about Ziph but a plea to be saved by the Name: Save me, O God, by Your name; judge my case by Your might. Strangers have risen; violent men hunt his life; they have not set God before them. Then the turn, after Selah: See -- God is the One who helps me; the Lord stands with those who hold my life up. He will turn the evil back on the men who were watching him, and cut them off in His truth. What David promises in return is a freewill offering and praise of the Name -- and here, for the only time in the psalm, he says LORD. He has already been delivered out of every trouble; his eye has seen it.

1.text: For the choir director. On stringed instruments. A maskil of David, when the Ziphites came and said to Saul, 'Is David not hiding among us?' Save me, O God, by Your name, and judge my case by Your might.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] on Neginoth [neginah -- stringed music], Maschil [maskil], A Psalm of David, when the Ziphims came [bo] and said [amar] to Saul, Doth not David hide [satar] himself with us? Save me, O God [Elohim], by thy name [shem], and judge [din] me by thy strength [geburah].
1.notes: The title names the informers: the Ziphites (H2130) came (H935) and told Saul (H7586) that David was hiding (H5641) among them -- the words of 1 Samuel 23:19, said again at 26:1. Elohim be-shimkha hoshieni (H430, H8034, H3467): Save me, O God, BY YOUR NAME -- not by a hiding place the Ziphites already knew. u-bi-gevuratekha tedineni (H1777, H1369): and by Your geburah, Your might, judge my case -- din, a legal plea, not a private revenge.

2.text: O God, hear my prayer; turn Your ear to the words my mouth is speaking.
2.amp: Hear [shama] my prayer [tephillah], O God [Elohim]; give ear [azan] to the words [emer] of my mouth [peh].
2.notes: Elohim shama tephillati (H8085, H8605, H430): hear my prayer, O God; haazinah le-imre-phi (H238, H561, H6310): give ear to the words of my mouth. Two verbs of hearing for a man whose hiding place has already been named out loud.

3.text: For strangers have risen against me, and ruthless men seek my life; they have not set God before them. Selah
3.amp: For strangers [zur] are risen up [qum] against me, and oppressors [arits -- ruthless, violent] seek [baqash] after my soul [nephesh]: they have not set [sum] God [Elohim] before them. Selah.
3.notes: ki zarim qamu alai (H2114, H6965): strangers have RISEN against me -- zur, the outsider, though the Ziphites were Judahites; they had made themselves foreign to him. ve-aritsim biqshu naphshi (H6184, H1245, H5315): ruthless men seek my life. lo samu Elohim le-negedam (H7760, H430): they have not set God before them. Selah (H5542). The charge under the betrayal is not geography. It is atheism in practice.

4.text: See -- God is the One who helps me; the Lord stands with those who hold my life up.
4.amp: Behold, God [Elohim] is mine helper [azar]: the Lord [Adonai] is with them that uphold [samak -- lean, support] my soul [nephesh].
4.notes: hinneh Elohim ozer li (H430, H5826): Behold -- God is my helper. Adonai be-somkhe naphshi (H136, H5564, H5315): the Lord -- Adonai, Master -- is with those who samak my soul, who lean their weight in to hold it up. Helper and upholders: he is not arguing that he is alone with God, but that God has put people under his life.

5.text: He will turn the evil back on those who watch me; in Your truth, cut them off.
5.amp: He shall reward [shub] evil [ra] unto mine enemies ['those that observe me', the KJV margin]: cut them off in thy truth [emeth].
5.notes: yashiv ha-ra le-shorerai (H7725, H7451, H8324): He will TURN BACK the evil on those who watch me -- the margin's 'those that observe me', the lookouts, not a generic foe. The verb is doubled in the tagged text, shub upon shub: the evil they aimed comes home. ha-tzemitim be-amitteka (H6789, H571): cut them off in Your emeth, Your truth. He does not ask to do it himself.

6.text: I will bring You a freewill sacrifice, and I will give thanks to Your name, O LORD, because it is good.
6.amp: I will freely [nedabah -- freewill offering] sacrifice [zabach] unto You: I will praise [yadah] Your name [shem], O LORD [YHWH]; for it is good [tov].
6.notes: bi-nedabah ezbechah-lakh (H5071, H2076): with a nedabah, a freewill offering, I will sacrifice to You -- not the vow a trapped man makes, but a gift no one required. odeh shimkha YHWH ki-tov (H3034, H8034, H3068, H2896): I will praise Your name, O LORD, for it is good. The only YHWH in the psalm lands on the Name he asked to be saved by in verse 1.

7.text: For He has delivered me out of every trouble, and my eye has looked on my enemies.
7.amp: For He has delivered [natsal] me out of all trouble [tsarah]: and mine eye [ayin] has seen [raah] his desire upon mine enemies [oyeb].
7.notes: ki mi-kol-tsarah hitsilani (H5337, H6869): He has SNATCHED me out of every trouble -- past tense, as if the Ziphite report has already failed. u-be-oyebai raatah eni (H5869, H7200, H341): and my eye has seen upon my enemies. He does not gloat over a corpse; he has seen the outcome with his own eye, which is the Hebrew way of saying the deliverance was not a rumor.
